diagnosis.what_is_wrong: No kernel evidence establishes a host or service fault behind the coding task’s longer completion time. There is a real, brief system-activity trough, but CPU use remains low, sampled wakeup-to-run delays are tiny, and the trace shows no supporting disk or network blockage; the later python3 workload is actively consuming CPU rather than stalled.
diagnosis.evidence: Compared full-span event rates and the 03:17:26–31 baseline with the 03:17:31–33 trough using the workers’ run_python/event-index results: sched_switch fell 77% (1091→248/s), sched_wakeup 78% (533→120/s), sched_stat_runtime 73% (916→245/s), and irq_softirq_entry 68% (606→195/s). The trough was not an obvious timestamp hole: timestamped records and CPU IDs 0–3 remained represented, and raw lines continued through it. But the full-trace sched_stat_runtime attribution shows only 0.148 CPU-seconds/second before and 0.226 during the later python3 phase; python3 accounts for 3.155 CPU-seconds over 16 seconds (about 0.20 core), not host saturation. In the raw samples around 03:17:35, a claude wakeup was followed by a switch about 16.6 μs later. Disk evidence did not show a latency buildup (sampled block issue/complete durations were about 0.01 ms), and network event counts were low. The task’s runtime name is not a unique service identity; the only observed namespace was pid_ns 4026531836. The check that would support CPU starvation—long wakeup-to-switch delays or a much higher CPU runtime rate—was run in the sampled interval and was not observed. Direct ctf_lines access failed, so raw-line checks used the workers’ run_python get_lines output.
diagnosis.window_evidence: This is the bounded system-activity trough, not a confirmed fault interval: the per-100-ms series drop sharply at 03:17:31.500 (sched_switch 61 to 16; sched_wakeup 29 to 8) and stay low through 03:17:33.500; activity rebounds at 03:17:33.600, with sched_switch reaching 132 then 307 at 03:17:33.800. Cross-series rates were compared against 03:17:26–31, and the sampled event streams remained populated during the trough.
